name: Geo-KTF
description: Geo-KTF is a platform-independent framework which maps geospatial knowledge to computational tools; it aims to help users find suitable tools, compare equivalent implementations across platforms, and turn concepts into executable workflows. Generally, it includes six pillars via a practical path: Understand foundations (Basic Geospatial Knowledge), Act with operations (Analytical Capabilities), Apply reusable workflows (Workflow), Ensure quality (Validation), Deliver outputs (Output), and Enable the stack via providers (Provider Registry).

children.name: Basic Geospatial Knowledge
Relationship
children.description: How features relate through overlay, topology, distance, connectivity, scale, and uncertainty.

children.name: Overlay
children.description: Overlay is the set of geometric operations that cut, merge, or reshape features by how they share space (buffer, clip, intersection, union, difference, dissolve). Use it when you need new geometries that answer “where do these layers interact?” Common tools include Buffer, Clip, Intersection, Union, Difference, Dissolve, and geopandas.overlay().

children.name: Adjacency
children.description: Adjacency describes whether features touch or share a boundary without one containing the other. Use it to find neighbours, shared borders, or topology between adjacent polygons and lines. Common tools include ST_Touches, ST_Overlaps, ST_Crosses, and Extract by location.

children.name: Containment
children.description: Containment is the inside/outside relationship between features (contains, within, clip-to-boundary). Use it for points-in-polygons, zoning checks, and coverage tests. Common tools include ST_Contains, ST_Within, Clip, and Extract by location.

children.name: Distance
children.description: Distance measures how far features are from each other in coordinate or ground units. Use it for proximity, nearest-neighbour, and neighbourhood definitions that are metric rather than purely topological. Common tools include Distance Matrix, Distance to nearest hub, ST_Distance, ST_DWithin, and Join attributes by nearest.

children.name: Connectivity
children.description: Connectivity asks whether places are linked by a traversable network path, not just by straight-line nearness. Use it for routing, service reach, and corridor questions on roads or other graphs. Common tools include pgr_dijkstra, pgr_aStar, pgr_drivingDistance, and openrouteservice directions.

children.name: Scale
children.description: Scale is about how much detail a dataset keeps and at what resolution phenomena are represented. Use it when generalising maps, choosing cell size, or building multi-resolution pyramids so analysis matches the question. Common tools include Simplify, Generalize, Create grid, gdaladdo, and gdalbuildvrt.

children.name: Uncertainty
children.description: Uncertainty means locations or values are not known exactly and may vary randomly or vaguely. Use it when sampling, testing sensitivity, or avoiding false certainty in maps. Common tools include Random points in extent, Random points in polygons, and Random selection.

children.name: Data Models
children.description: Core geospatial data structures and their processing ecosystems.

children.name: Vector
children.description: Vector data stores discrete features as points, lines, or polygons with attributes. Use it for crisp boundaries, networks of features, and rich tabular properties. Common tools include ogrinfo, ogr2ogr, and GeoPandas read/write functions.

children.name: Raster
children.description: Raster data stores values on a regular grid of cells (imagery, elevation, land cover). Use it for continuous fields and pixel-based analysis. Common tools include gdalinfo, gdal_translate, gdalwarp, gdalbuildvrt, and rasterio.open().

children.name: Point Cloud
children.description: A point cloud is a dense set of 3D points, often from LiDAR or photogrammetry. Use it to capture fine surface structure before deriving DEMs or meshes. Common tools include PDAL pipeline stages such as readers.las, filters, and writers.

children.name: Mesh
children.description: A mesh represents surfaces as connected faces and edges, often for 3D visualisation or simulation. Use it when terrain or urban surfaces are more complex than a simple DEM grid. Common tools include Mesh Calculator and mesh export tools in QGIS.

children.name: TIN
children.description: A TIN (triangulated irregular network) models a surface from irregular points connected as triangles. Use it to interpolate terrain or other fields while keeping sample locations. Common tools include TIN Interpolation, Delaunay triangulation, Create grid, and gdal_grid.

children.name: DEM
children.description: A DEM (digital elevation model) is a raster of ground (or surface) height. Use it as the base for slope, aspect, hydrology, viewsheds, and hillshade. Common tools include gdaldem derivatives, gdal_contour, and gdal_viewshed.

children.name: Network
children.description: A network is a graph of nodes and edges with costs such as length or travel time. Use it when movement follows roads or pipes rather than straight lines. Common tools include pgRouting functions such as pgr_dijkstra and pgr_drivingDistance.

children.name: Temporal Data
children.description: Temporal data attaches times or date ranges to geographic observations so change can be tracked. Use it for multi-date imagery, event histories, and trend analysis. Common tools include gdalbuildvrt for time stacks, GeoParquet, and time-aware vector reads.

children.name: Hex Grid
children.description: A hex grid divides space into regular hexagonal cells for aggregation and comparison. Use it to summarise points or rates with less directional bias than square grids. Common tools include Create grid plus spatial joins such as geopandas.sjoin() or ST_Intersects.

children.name: Trajectory
children.description: A trajectory is an ordered path of locations through time for a moving object. Use it for mobility, GPS tracks, and route-behaviour analysis. Common tools include MovingPandas, Shortest Path, pgr_dijkstra, pgr_dijkstraVia, pgr_aStar, and openrouteservice directions.

children.name: 3D
children.description: 3D geospatial models add height or full volumetric structure beyond flat maps. Use them for buildings, terrain scenes, and height-aware planning. Common tools include QGIS 3D Map View and mesh export utilities.

children.name: Spatial Indexing
children.description: Spatial indexing organises geometries so searches and joins do not scan every feature. Use it to keep large spatial queries fast in databases and analytics engines. Common tools include CREATE INDEX USING GIST, ST_GeoHash, PostGIS, ST_Intersects, and DuckDB Spatial.

children.name: Knowledge Graph
children.description: A spatial knowledge graph links places and concepts as typed relationships that can be queried semantically (often with GeoSPARQL). Use it when meaning and links matter as much as coordinates. Common tools include GeoSPARQL, RDFLib, Apache Jena, Apache Jena Fuseki, GraphDB, and Ontop.

children.name: Topology
children.description: Topology is a data model that records how features share boundaries and connect, not only their shapes. Use it to enforce adjacency rules, catch gaps/overlaps, and support network-ready geometry. Common tools include Check Geometries, Fix Geometries, Delete Duplicate Geometries, ST_Touches, ST_Overlaps, and ST_Crosses.

children.name: Coverage
children.description: A coverage maps positions in space (and often time) to attribute values, typically as continuous fields such as temperature or elevation surfaces. Use it when analysis needs values “everywhere” rather than discrete features. Common tools include gdalinfo, gdal_translate, rasterio.open(), COG, STAC, and gdalbuildvrt.

children.name: Coordinate Reference Systems
children.description: How location is referenced, transformed, and validated.

children.name: Geographic
children.description: A geographic CRS locates positions on the Earth ellipsoid (latitude/longitude); a projected CRS maps them to a plane. Use the right type so distance, area, and alignment stay meaningful. Common tools include pyproj.CRS, geopandas.to_crs(), ST_Transform, and gdalwarp.

children.name: Datums
children.description: A datum is the reference frame that defines where coordinates sit relative to the Earth. Use correct datum transformations to avoid metre- to tens-of-metre shifts between layers. Common tools include pyproj.Transformer, ST_Transform, gdalwarp, and projinfo.

children.name: Vertical CRS
children.description: A vertical CRS defines how heights and depths are referenced (ellipsoid, geoid, or local). Use it when elevation must be consistent for engineering, flood, or 3D work. Common tools include pyproj.CRS, projinfo, gdalinfo, and ST_Transform where vertical operations are supported.

children.name: Units
children.description: CRS units are the linear or angular units of coordinates (degrees, metres, feet). Use them consciously so buffers and lengths are not computed in degrees by mistake. Common tools include pyproj.CRS, projinfo, ST_Length, and ST_Area.

children.name: Common CRS Errors
children.description: Common CRS errors include missing CRS tags, wrong axis order, wrong datum, and confusing assign-versus-reproject. Fix them early with inspection and the correct assign or transform tools. Common tools include pyproj.CRS, projinfo, gdalinfo/ogrinfo/rio info, geopandas.set_crs()/to_crs(), ST_SRID/ST_SetSRID/ST_Transform, Assign projection, Reproject Layer, and gdalwarp.

children.name: Data Quality
children.description: Trust, fitness for use, and documentation of geospatial data.

children.name: Metadata
children.description: Metadata is descriptive information about a dataset (what it is, CRS, extent, how it was made). Use it to judge fitness for purpose before analysis. Common tools include gdalinfo, ogrinfo, rio info, and dataset openers that surface schema and CRS.

children.name: Lineage
children.description: Lineage is the processing history of how a dataset or result was produced. Use it for reproducibility, auditing, and teaching. Common tools include QGIS Processing History, Processing Log, qgis_process, and Model Designer.

children.name: Precision
children.description: Precision is how finely locations and values are represented (resolution, decimals, generalisation)—not whether they are correct. Use appropriate precision to balance detail, file size, and meaningful differences. Common tools include gdalinfo, Simplify, Generalize, Create grid, gdaladdo, and Snap geometries to grid.

children.name: Validity
children.description: Geometric validity means features obey structural rules needed for overlays and databases. Use validity checks to stop silent failures before analysis. Common tools include Check Geometries, Fix Geometries, ST_IsValid, and the QGIS Geometry Checker.

children.name: Standards
children.description: Geospatial standards provide common rules for describing data, reporting quality, encoding metadata, and publishing catalogue records. They make datasets easier to discover, validate, exchange, and reuse across organisations and software. This category covers metadata models, XML/RDF encodings, quality standards, regional metadata profiles, catalogue interfaces, and tools that create or manage standards-based records.

children.name: Uncertainty Modeling
children.description: Uncertainty modeling represents error, vagueness, or random variation instead of treating every value as exact. Use it when decisions need confidence ranges or soft thresholds. Common tools include Fuzzy Overlay, Monte Carlo simulation, and random sampling tools.

children.name: Spatial Analysis
children.description: Core analytical families spanning vector, raster, network, and terrain.

children.name: Vector Analysis
children.description: Vector analysis is the family of geometry and attribute operations on points, lines, and polygons. Use it for overlays, buffers, dissolves, joins, and proximity on discrete features. Common tools include Buffer, Clip, Intersection, Dissolve, and spatial joins.

children.name: Raster Analysis
children.description: Raster analysis applies map algebra, resampling, proximity, and related operations on grids. Use it for indices, reclassification, distance surfaces, and areal transfers to new zones. Common tools include Raster Calculator, gdal_calc, gdal_proximity, and tobler.area_interpolate().

children.name: Terrain Analysis
children.description: Terrain analysis derives landform metrics from elevation (slope, aspect, ruggedness, viewshed, contours). Use it for hazard, ecology, engineering, and landscape characterisation. Common tools include gdaldem slope/aspect/hillshade/TRI/TPI, gdal_contour, and gdal_viewshed.

children.name: Network Analysis
children.description: Network analysis solves path, cost, and catchment problems on connected graphs. Use it for logistics, emergency response, and service planning on roads or similar networks. Common tools include Shortest Path, Service Area, pgr_dijkstra, and openrouteservice directions.

children.goal: Build the foundations: data models, CRS, spatial relationships, quality, and core analysis ideas.

children.name: Analytical Capabilities
Data Inspection
children.description: Data inspection is checking structure, CRS, extent, schema, and content before analysis. Use it to catch bad inputs early and avoid wasted runs. Common tools include gdalinfo, ogrinfo, GeoPandas readers, rasterio.open(), and PDAL pipeline.

children.name: Data Acquisition
children.description: Data acquisition is capturing or collecting new geospatial observations in the field or from imagery and VGI. Use it when you need fresh, georeferenced primary data. Common tools include QField, ODK Collect, Georeferencer, GPSBabel, OpenDroneMap, iD Editor, and JOSM.

children.name: Data Conversion
children.description: Data conversion transforms formats, encodings, and storage targets while trying to preserve meaning. Use it to move data between desktop, database, and cloud ecosystems. Common tools include ogr2ogr, gdal_translate, gdalwarp, gdalbuildvrt, and GeoPandas writers.

children.name: CRS Management
children.description: CRS management assigns, inspects, and reprojects coordinate reference systems. Use it so layers align and measurements stay valid. Common tools include pyproj, GeoPandas CRS methods, ST_Transform, Assign projection, and gdalwarp.

children.name: Vector Processing
children.description: Vector processing runs geometry and attribute operations that reshape vector layers. Use it as the day-to-day geoprocessing toolbox for overlays and edits. Common tools include Buffer, Clip, Intersection, Dissolve, Merge, Simplify, and nearest joins.

children.name: Raster Processing
children.description: Raster processing covers resampling, algebra, mosaics, proximity, and raster–vector conversion. Use it to prepare imagery and surfaces for modelling and maps. Common tools include Raster Calculator, gdal_calc, gdal_translate, gdalwarp, and gdal_polygonize.

children.name: Database Processing
children.description: Database processing reads, writes, and computes spatial data inside a spatial database. Use it for scalable analysis close to stored data with indexes. Common tools include PostGIS ST_ functions, DuckDB ST_Read, and GeoPandas PostGIS I/O.

children.name: Spatial SQL
children.description: Spatial SQL expresses spatial filters and overlays as declarative queries. Use it for reproducible, set-based analysis on large tables. Common tools include ST_Intersects, ST_Contains, ST_Buffer, ST_DWithin, ST_Intersection, and ST_Transform.

children.name: Geocoding
children.description: Geocoding converts place names or addresses to coordinates (and reverse geocoding does the opposite). Use it to put tabular records on the map. Common tools include Nominatim, openrouteservice geocoding, Google Geocoding API, and ArcGIS Geocoding Service.

children.name: Routing
children.description: Routing computes paths, costs, and turn-by-turn directions on a transportation network. Use it when travel follows roads rather than straight lines. Common tools include Shortest Path, pgr_dijkstra, pgr_aStar, pgr_KSP, and openrouteservice directions.

children.name: Accessibility
children.description: Accessibility measures how reachable places are under time, distance, or impedance limits. Use it for equity, service coverage, and catchment planning. Common tools include Service Area, openrouteservice isochrones/matrices, Distance Matrix, and pgr_drivingDistance.

children.name: Location-Allocation
children.description: Location-allocation chooses facility sites and assigns demand to them to cut travel cost or raise coverage. Use it for siting schools, clinics, warehouses, and similar facilities. Common tools include v.net.alloc, OD matrices, Service Area, Distance Matrix, and ortools.routing.
tools: OD Matrix from Layers as Lines (m:n)

children.name: Remote Sensing
children.description: Remote sensing processes Earth observation imagery into analysis-ready layers and thematic maps. Use it for land cover, change, and feature extraction from satellites or drones. Common tools include GDAL/Rasterio/OTB utilities, OpenDroneMap, classifiers, and confusion-matrix tools.

children.name: Spatial Statistics
children.description: Spatial statistics quantify pattern, clustering, autocorrelation, and density in geographic data. Use it to test whether observed patterns are structured or likely random. Common tools include esda.Moran, Moran_Local, Geary, GetisOrd, libpysal.weights, and Heatmap (KDE).

children.name: Spatial Regression
children.description: Spatial regression models relationships while accounting for spatial dependence or local variation. Use it when ordinary regression residuals are spatially autocorrelated or effects change across space. Common tools include spreg.OLS, ML_Lag, ML_Error, mgwr.GWR, and libpysal.weights.

children.name: Point Pattern Analysis
children.description: Point pattern analysis describes whether events cluster, disperse, or look random in space. Use it for crime, disease, retail, or any event-dot map beyond a simple heatmap. Common tools include pointpats.PointPattern, centrography, Heatmap (KDE), and DBSCAN.

children.name: Multi-Criteria Evaluation
children.description: Multi-criteria evaluation (MCE) combines weighted criteria layers to rank or select suitable places. Use it for suitability and site screening with several factors. Common tools include Weighted Overlay, Fuzzy Overlay, Reclassify by table, and raster calculators.

children.name: Spatial Interpolation
children.description: Spatial interpolation predicts values at unsampled locations to build a continuous surface. Use it to map sparse measurements such as temperature, pollution, or elevation samples. Common tools include IDW, TIN, multilevel B-spline, thin-plate spline, gdal_grid, and PyKrige.

children.name: Clustering
children.description: Clustering groups observations by location and/or attributes into similar sets. Use it to find natural groupings without drawing boundaries by hand. Common tools include DBSCAN, K-means, HDBSCAN, scikit-learn clusterers, and PostGIS ST_Cluster* functions.

children.name: Cartography
children.description: Cartography designs how spatial information is seen through symbols, colour, labels, themes, and layout. Use it to communicate patterns clearly without misleading readers. Common tools include QGIS Style Manager, symbol/label tools, graduated/categorized renderers, Print Layout, contours, and hillshade.

children.name: Space-Time Analysis
children.description: Space-time analysis studies how locations, attributes, or movements change through time. Use it for dynamics, animation, and multi-date comparison. Common tools include MovingPandas, QGIS Temporal Controller, GeoParquet, and multi-date VRT stacks.

children.name: Trajectory Analysis
children.description: Trajectory analysis studies ordered movement paths and travel behaviour. Use it for GPS tracks, fleet routes, and path comparison. Common tools include MovingPandas, Shortest Path, and pgRouting/openrouteservice path tools.

children.name: Geocomputation
children.description: Geocomputation uses simulation and iterative models (agents, cellular automata, visual models) for spatial processes. Use it when static GIS overlays cannot capture evolving behaviour. Common tools include mesa, NetLogo, Cellular Automata concepts, and QGIS Model Designer.

children.name: Terrain Analysis
children.description: Terrain analysis derives landform metrics from elevation (slope, aspect, ruggedness, contours, viewshed). Use it for hazard, engineering, ecology, and landscape characterisation. Common tools include gdaldem slope/aspect/hillshade/TRI/TPI, gdal_contour, and gdal_viewshed.

children.name: Network Analysis
children.description: Network analysis solves path, cost, and catchment problems on connected graphs. Use it when movement must follow roads or similar networks rather than straight lines. Common tools include Shortest Path, Service Area, pgr_dijkstra, pgr_aStar, pgr_KSP, pgr_drivingDistance, and openrouteservice directions.

children.name: Proximity Analysis
children.description: Proximity analysis measures how near features are using buffers, distances, nearest joins, and proximity rasters. Use it for setbacks, service reach in Euclidean space, and exposure screening. Common tools include Buffer, Distance Matrix, ST_Distance, ST_DWithin, gdal_proximity, and nearest-join tools.

children.name: Density Analysis
children.description: Density analysis estimates how intensely events or features concentrate across space. Use it for hotspots, demand surfaces, and grid-based counts. Common tools include Heatmap (KDE), Create grid with spatial joins, DBSCAN clustering, and ST_ClusterDBSCAN.

children.name: Feature Extraction
children.description: Feature extraction turns imagery or dense surfaces into discrete GIS features (buildings, objects, polygons). Use it to move from pixels to vector objects for downstream analysis. Common tools include SAM/samgeo, gdal_polygonize, OTB classifiers, OpenDroneMap, and Structure from Motion.

children.name: Data Cleaning
children.description: Data cleaning repairs and tidies geometries and attributes before analysis. Use it to remove invalid shapes, duplicates, schema mismatches, and digitising noise. Common tools include Check/Fix Geometries, Delete Duplicate Geometries, Snap geometries to grid, Refactor Fields, and Simplify.

children.goal: Carry out software-neutral operations to inspect, transform, analyse, and map spatial data.

children.name: Workflow
Site Selection
children.description: Site selection is a workflow that combines spatial criteria to shortlist candidate locations. Use it for facilities or interventions that must meet several geographic rules. Common tools include Buffer, Clip, Intersection, and Weighted Overlay.

children.name: Suitability Analysis
children.description: Suitability analysis scores places against weighted criteria so alternatives can be ranked. Use it to turn policy or expert weights into a comparable map. Common tools include Raster Calculator, Weighted Overlay, Fuzzy Overlay, and Model Designer.

children.name: Catchment Analysis
children.description: Catchment analysis delineates the area served by a facility or contributing to a downstream point. Use it for service areas and watershed-style reasoning. Common tools include Service Area, pgr_drivingDistance, and openrouteservice isochrones.

children.name: Accessibility Analysis
children.description: Accessibility analysis evaluates how easily people or goods reach destinations under travel constraints. Use it for equity and coverage studies. Common tools include Service Area, Distance Matrix, and openrouteservice isochrones/matrices.

children.name: Demographic Enrichment
children.description: Demographic enrichment attaches population or socioeconomic attributes to spatial features. Use it when analysis needs census-like context not stored on the geometry. Common tools include Join attributes by location, geopandas.sjoin(), ST_Contains, and ST_Intersects.

children.name: Hazard Assessment
children.description: Hazard assessment maps exposure and susceptibility using terrain and thematic overlays. Use it for screening and preparedness communication. Common tools include gdaldem slope/aspect, Intersection, Clip, and Buffer.

children.name: Environmental Assessment
children.description: Environmental assessment evaluates conditions and impacts with buffers, proximity, overlays, and raster criteria. Use it for screening sensitivity and constraints. Common tools include Buffer, Clip, Intersection, gdal_proximity, and raster calculators.

children.name: Infrastructure Planning
children.description: Infrastructure planning uses networks, catchments, and proximity to site facilities and corridors. Use it when cost, access, and spatial suitability must be balanced. Common tools include Shortest Path, Service Area, Distance Matrix, Buffer, and routing engines.

children.name: Change Detection
children.description: Change detection compares multi-temporal datasets to find where and how landscapes changed. Use it for monitoring land cover, urban growth, or disturbance. Common tools include gdalwarp, gdal_translate, gdal_calc, BandMath, and gdalbuildvrt.

children.name: Hydrological Analysis
children.description: Hydrological analysis models surface drainage from filled DEMs through flow and watersheds. Use it for flood, watershed, and drainage design studies. Common tools include Fill sinks, Flow direction, Flow accumulation, Watershed, and Channel network.

children.name: Visibility Analysis
children.description: Visibility analysis finds what can be seen from observer points given terrain occlusion. Use it for towers, scenic assessment, and security line-of-sight. Common tools include Viewshed and gdal_viewshed.

children.name: Remote Sensing Classification
children.description: Remote sensing classification assigns thematic classes to pixels or objects from imagery. Use it to produce land-cover or similar maps from EO data. Common tools include OTB TrainImagesClassifier, KMeansClassification, SAM, and BandMath.

children.name: Urban Growth Analysis
children.description: Urban growth analysis tracks expansion and intensification of development over time. Use it for planning insight from multi-date imagery and pattern metrics. Common tools include gdalwarp, gdal_calc, Heatmap (KDE), and spatial statistics tools.

children.name: Flood Risk Analysis
children.description: Flood risk analysis combines drainage modelling with overlays to screen exposure near channels, basins, or low areas. Use it for preparedness screening and planning communication. Common tools include Fill sinks, Flow direction/accumulation, Watershed, Buffer, Intersection, Raster Calculator, and gdal_proximity.

children.name: Least-Cost Corridor Analysis
children.description: Least-cost corridor analysis finds preferred routes that minimise travel impedance across networks or cost rasters. Use it for infrastructure corridors, wildlife passages, and access planning. Common tools include Shortest Path, pgr_dijkstra, gdal_proximity, Weighted Overlay, Raster Calculator, and Buffer.

children.name: Land Cover Mapping
children.description: Land cover mapping is an end-to-end workflow from imagery preparation to classified maps and accuracy checks. Use it to produce thematic land-cover products for monitoring and planning. Common tools include OTB TrainImagesClassifier/KMeans/BandMath, gdal_calc, confusion-matrix tools, and SAM.

children.name: Emergency Response Planning
children.description: Emergency response planning evaluates how quickly responders or people can reach critical locations under network constraints. Use it for station coverage, evacuation routing, and response-time scenarios. Common tools include Service Area, Shortest Path, pgr_dijkstra, pgr_drivingDistance, and openrouteservice isochrones/directions.

children.name: Solar Site Assessment
children.description: Solar site assessment screens candidate locations using terrain orientation, shading, and visibility-related criteria. Use it for rooftop or ground-mounted solar screening before detailed engineering. Common tools include gdaldem slope/aspect/hillshade, Viewshed, gdal_viewshed, Raster Calculator, and Weighted Overlay.

children.name: Habitat Suitability Mapping
children.description: Habitat suitability mapping ranks places for species or conservation goals from weighted environmental criteria. Use it for conservation planning and impact screening. Common tools include Weighted Overlay, Fuzzy Overlay, Reclassify by table, raster calculators, Buffer, Clip, and Intersection.

children.goal: Combine operations into reusable end-to-end workflows for common geospatial tasks.

children.name: Validation
Geometry Validation
children.description: Geometry validation detects and repairs invalid vector geometries. Use it before overlays, joins, or database loads. Common tools include Check Geometries, Fix Geometries, ST_IsValid, and Shapely is_valid.

children.name: CRS Validation
children.description: CRS validation confirms that coordinate systems are assigned and transformed correctly. Use it to prevent alignment and measurement errors. Common tools include pyproj, projinfo, Reproject Layer, Assign projection, and gdalinfo/ogrinfo.

children.name: Metadata Validation
children.description: Metadata validation checks whether descriptive information is complete and consistent with the data. Use it before publishing or handing datasets to others. Common tools include gdalinfo, ogrinfo, rio info, and GeoPandas readers.

children.name: Schema Validation
children.description: Schema validation checks fields, types, and table structure before joins or loads. Use it to stop automation and database failures from mismatched attributes. Common tools include ogrinfo, GeoPandas readers, and Refactor Fields.

children.name: Topology Validation
children.description: Topology validation checks relationships between features (gaps, overlaps, shared borders), not only single-geometry validity. Use it before overlays and network building. Common tools include ST_Touches/Overlaps/Crosses, Extract by location, and Check Geometries.

children.name: Statistical Validation
children.description: Statistical validation uses spatial statistics to test whether patterns are structured or consistent with expectations. Use it as a quality gate for claims about clustering or dependence. Common tools include esda Moran/Geary/GetisOrd and libpysal.weights.

children.name: Accuracy Assessment
children.description: Accuracy assessment compares classified or predicted maps with reference samples. Use it to report how close results are to truth (distinct from precision/resolution). Common tools include OTB ComputeConfusionMatrix, scikit-learn.metrics, Extract by location, and Random points in polygons.

children.name: Result Validation
children.description: Result validation audits outputs against methods, parameters, and processing history. Use it before publishing or handing results to another analyst. Common tools include QGIS Processing History/Log, qgis_process, and field statistics reports.

children.goal: Check that data, CRS, geometry, logic, and results are valid, consistent, and trustworthy.

children.name: Output
Tables
children.description: Tables are tabular exports of attributes and summaries. Use them for spreadsheets, statistics, and non-map review. Common tools include GeoPandas writers, ogr2ogr, and field statistics tools.

children.name: GIS Files
children.description: GIS files package geometries, attributes, and georeferencing for exchange between systems. Use them as the portable handoff between analysis and reuse. Common tools include ogr2ogr, gdal_translate/warp/buildvrt/merge, and GeoPandas file writers.

children.name: Maps
children.description: Map-centred deliverables: cartographic map products and narrative story maps.

children.name: Cartographic Maps
children.description: Cartographic maps are designed map sheets or images with symbols, labels, legend, and layout. Use them for print, PDF, or image export when the deliverable is a map—not a scrollable story. Common tools include QGIS Print Layout, Style Manager, symbol/label tools, graduated/categorized renderers, Contour, and hillshade.

children.name: Story Maps
children.description: Story maps are guided multimedia narratives under the Maps family that sequence maps with text, photos, and media. Unlike cartographic maps, they walk readers through a storyline rather than presenting a single map sheet. Common tools include ArcGIS StoryMaps and Knight Lab StoryMapJS.

children.name: Tiles
children.description: Tiles are pre-cut map images or vector tiles served by zoom level for fast web mapping. Use them to publish large maps online without sending full datasets to every client. Common tools include gdal_retile, gdaladdo, GeoServer, QGIS Server, MapLibre GL JS, Leaflet, and OpenLayers.

children.name: Cloud-Native Products
children.description: Cloud-native products are spatial datasets organised for efficient cloud storage and partial access. Use them when sharing large rasters or vector tables via object storage and modern analytics. Common tools and formats include COG, GeoParquet, STAC, gdal_translate, geopandas.to_parquet(), and AWS.

children.name: Metadata Records
children.description: Metadata records describe datasets and services so others can discover and judge them. Use them when publishing outputs into an SDI or open-data catalogue. Common tools and specs include GeoNetwork, pygeometa, ISO 19115/19139, INSPIRE Metadata, and OGC CSW.

children.name: Reports
children.description: Reports combine narrative, figures, and methods for stakeholders. Use them when a map alone is not enough explanation. Common tools include QGIS Reports and QGIS Print Layout.

children.name: Dashboards
children.description: Dashboards are interactive operational views of spatial results. Use them for monitoring and exploration beyond static maps. Common tools include QGIS Server, GeoServer, Leaflet, MapLibre GL JS, and OpenLayers.

children.name: APIs
children.description: APIs expose spatial data and processing programmatically. Use them to integrate GIS results into other applications. Common tools and services include QGIS Server, GeoServer, PostGIS, DuckDB Spatial, and routing/geocoding APIs.

children.goal: Produce tables, files, maps, reports, APIs, and dashboards for sharing and decision-making.

children.name: Provider Registry
Geospatial Libraries
children.description: Geospatial libraries are the software engines behind many GIS operations (I/O, geometry, raster, routing). Use this registry to see which stack implements a capability. Common entries include GDAL/OGR, GeoPandas, PostGIS, PDAL, PySAL, and routing libraries.

children.name: Cloud
children.description: Cloud providers and formats support scalable storage and compute for large spatial data. Use them when desktop machines are not enough. Common entries include AWS, Google Earth Engine, ArcGIS Online, COG, GeoParquet, and Apache Sedona.

children.name: SDI / Catalogs
children.description: SDI and catalogs make datasets discoverable through metadata search and standard access. Use them to find and publish organisational or open data. Common entries include GeoNetwork, CKAN, STAC, pystac, and Planetary Computer.

children.name: Notebooks
children.description: Notebooks are literate computing environments mixing code, text, and figures. Use them for reproducible teaching and analysis workflows. Common entries include Jupyter Notebook, Google Colab, and ArcGIS Notebooks.

children.name: Development
children.description: Development covers languages and automation used to build GIS scripts and apps. Use them to move beyond one-off GUI clicks. Common entries include Python for GIS, R for GIS, JavaScript for GIS, Model Designer, and qgis_process.

children.name: Basemap
children.description: Basemap providers supply reference geography and open contextual layers. Use them as background or boundary inputs for analysis and maps. Common entries include OpenStreetMap, Google Maps, Overture Maps, Natural Earth, and open data APIs.

children.name: Web Mapping
children.description: Web mapping providers are clients and servers for interactive online maps. Use them to publish results beyond desktop GIS. Common entries include MapLibre GL JS, Leaflet, OpenLayers, GeoServer, and QGIS Server.

children.name: AI
children.description: AI providers are machine-learning and deep-learning frameworks applied to geospatial tasks such as classification, detection, and segmentation. Use them when patterns are learned from labelled (or pretrained) data rather than only hand-coded GIS rules. Common tools include scikit-learn, XGBoost/LightGBM, PyTorch/TensorFlow/Keras, TorchGeo, Raster Vision, YOLO, Transformers, and SAM/samgeo.

children.goal: Access the libraries, platforms, catalogues, and data sources that power the analysis stack.
